product.olivetti-echos-44-color.summary: The highest-performance Echos in the 1994 brochure targeted demanding graphics applications.
product.olivetti-echos-44-color.history: In October 1994, Olivetti’s brochure placed the Echos 44 Color above the 43 Color as the business option for more demanding graphics work. Computer Business Review reported a UK price of £2,100 and that shipments began in October.
product.olivetti-echos-44-color.architec: Expansion cards could add connectivity. The brochure documents a VESA local video bus and room for two Type II PCMCIA cards or one Type III card. The brochure specifies a 40 MHz i486DX2, while the Danmarks Tekniske Museum photograph record identifies its NB40 as a 33 MHz i486SX.
product.olivetti-echos-44-color.verified: The configuration was checked against the cited sources. BluMach validation is pending.
product.olivetti-echos-44-color.limitati: Firmware verification and boot tests are pending.
product.olivetti-echos-44-color.brochure: Olivetti, Echos Portable Personal Computers, 3994073P-00, 10/1994, pp. 2, 4.
product.olivetti-echos-44-color.museum: Danmarks Tekniske Museum, Echos 44 Color NB40 photograph record.
product.olivetti-echos-44-color.market: Computer Business Review, 4 October 1994, Olivetti launches new range of terracotta notebook computers.
